summary: Billing tier upgrade triggered immediate quota refresh and short-lived 429s for live streaming keys
description: Issue summary: Customer reports receiving a flood of 429 responses across long-lived streaming sessions immediately after upgrading their billing plan/commit. Impact: intermittent production failures for user-facing streaming features; several sessions observed to disconnect and reconnect, then hit soft 429s for ~3–7 minutes. Environment: Production, us-east primary with eu-west failover. Account activity: BrightData.ai upgraded from Dedicated Starter to Enterprise Reserved on 2026-03-10 14:02 UTC. They expected quota expansion to be instantaneous and non-disruptive. Observed behavior: quota counters appear to be reset but some token-buckets temporarily under-accounted during the migration window, causing short-lived rejections on ongoing websocket/http2 streaming sessions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Have long-lived streaming connections (http2 multiplex or websocket) active during a billing plan upgrade (simulate plan change via account admin).
2) Trigger the billing tier change in the Console or via partner billing API at scale (multiple API keys tied to same org).
3) Observe active connections for 5–10 minutes post-upgrade: some clients receive 429s with X-RateLimit-* headers showing lower-than-expected token counts or missing bucket headers.
4) New connections after upgrade get correct quotas; impact window seems limited to sessions that were already connected.

investigation_notes: Initial triage: migration job for billing->quota mapping initiated a 'replace' update rather than 'augment' for in-memory token-buckets used by live connections.
Hypothesis: token-bucket data migration path zeroes or temporarily reinitializes in-process bucket state for existing session objects when billing metadata is swapped in the control plane.
Observed pattern: HTTP/2 multiplexed streams and long-lived websockets had higher incidence than short-lived REST calls (consistent with per-connection in-memory bucket caching).
Correlated with deployment change: control-plane rollout v2026.03.10-rc3 included quota-engine change to support tiered burst windows; the migration job was included in the same deploy window.
comments: Customer (2026-03-10 14:15 UTC): We upgraded at 14:02 and saw immediate 429s on user sessions. New sessions look fine. Can you confirm this was expected?
Support (Maya Patel, 2026-03-10 14:22 UTC): Thanks — opening ticket and escalating to SRE. Please share a few sample connection IDs; we've asked for logs and a runbook check.

SRE (Ethan Garcia, 2026-03-10 15:05 UTC): We're seeing the migration job touching in-memory buckets. Reproduced locally with a small harness. Adding engineers responsible for quota-engine to investigate migration semantics.

Quota Eng (Lina Huang, 2026-03-10 16:12 UTC): Confirmed migration code path used a swap-and-init pattern. Patch prepared to perform a non-destructive merge for active-bucket entries. Will test in staging.
Customer (2026-03-11 09:04 UTC): Impacted ~1200 daily active streaming users; some reported reconnect loops. Appreciate ETA for fix.

SRE (2026-03-11 18:30 UTC): Hotfix deployed to control plane (quota-engine v2026.03.11-hotfix1). We backfilled active connections and triggered a reconciliation. Monitoring shows reduction in 429s to baseline.
root_cause_summary: A control-plane migration job associated with the billing-plan upgrade replaced active in-memory token-buckets for live connections instead of merging/updating them, temporarily reducing available tokens for established sessions and producing short-lived 429s.
resolution: Hotfix applied to quota-engine to perform a safe merge/update of active-bucket state during plan migrations. We performed a reconciliation job for BrightData.ai which restored expected token counts for active sessions. SRE added a guard to run migrations out-of-band or in a staged manner when active streaming sessions exceed a configurable threshold.
postmortem_followups: 1) Add migration-time safety checks: abort migration if active_stream_sessions > 2000 (configurable).
2) Add telemetry to track in-memory bucket replace events and emit alerting if replacement occurs during a billing change.
3) Update Console messaging and API docs to recommend performing plan upgrades during low-traffic windows for long-lived streaming workloads (short term mitigation).
4) Create a runbook entry for 'billing plan upgrade with active streams' to ensure ops coordinates a staged migration.
